# Live API fixtures

Real responses captured with `curl -sS --max-time 30 -A "sno-ball-dev/0.1 (github.com/FernForager/sno-ball)"` on 2026-10-07 (UTC times below). Each file is the body exactly as returned, re-serialized with 2-space indentation and no escaping of non-ASCII characters; nothing was removed or renamed. Nominatim requests were sent one at a time, 1.6 s apart. Wikidata SPARQL and Seattle/DNR ArcGIS queries were sent as GET requests.

Licences of the data inside: OpenStreetMap/Nominatim/Photon ODbL; Wikipedia CC BY-SA 4.0; Wikidata CC0; Macrostrat CC BY 4.0; GPlates (MERDITH2021 model) CC BY 4.0; WA DNR, Seattle GeoData (PDDL) and USGS public domain or open; OpenFreeMap style is open (see https://openfreemap.org).

## Notes on the responses (differences from docs/WA-PROBES.md and other surprises)

- **Nominatim search, Space Needle:** 2 hits. First is the building way 12903132 (`man_made=tower`), second is the node for "The Loupe Lounge" (a bar inside it). `extratags` is present on both; it is `null` on plain address hits (Walla Walla, the Spokane house way).
- **Nominatim search, 507 N Howard St Spokane:** the first hit is "Numerica Skate Ribbon" (`shop=ticket`, way 460674435, carries `wikidata`/`wikipedia` extratags); the plain address way 37178337 comes second. Address searches can return a POI before the address itself.
- **Nominatim search, outside WA with `bounded=1`:** returns `[]` (an empty array, HTTP 200), as expected.
- **Nominatim reverse at the Space Needle (zoom 18):** returns the bar node 3359850618, not the building way (matches the API report). Reverse at the Wedgwood point returns a parking way with an empty `name` and a `display_name` that starts with the road.
- **Photon:** `properties.county` is `King` (no "County" suffix), unlike Nominatim's `King County`. Results include `extent` (bbox) for ways.
- **WA DNR layer 11:** fields match WA-PROBES.md; the join key value looks like `Compiled | Qgt` (quad name, pipe, unit). The three sample points all sit on the `Compiled` quad.
- **WA DNR table 13:** the matched row has `DMU_100K_MAP_UNIT`, `DMU_100K_FULL_NAME`, `DMU_100K_AGE`, `DMU_100K_DESCRIPTION`, `DMU_100K_QUAD_NAME`, `DMU_FEATURE_QUAD_UNIT`, `DMU_100K_ID`, `GLOBALID`. `DMU_100K_FULL_NAME` can be `null` (Walla Walla, unit Qa, age "Quaternary"). The table also reports `displayFieldName: DMU_100K_NAME`, a field that is not in the row.
- **GPlates:** the single-time form returns a GeoJSON `MultiPoint`. The batched form (`times=20,50,100,...`) also returns HTTP 200: an object keyed by the time as a string (`"20"`, `"50"`, ...) whose values are `MultiPoint` objects. At 500 Ma the MERDITH2021 model returns the sentinel coordinate `[999.99, 999.99]`, meaning the point is not on any plate at that time, so callers must filter that value.
- **Seattle neighborhoods:** one polygon, `L_HOOD` "Queen Anne", `S_HOOD` "Lower Queen Anne", `S_HOOD_ALT_NAMES` "Uptown, Seattle Center". Service spatial reference is EPSG 2926 (WA State Plane North, feet) even with `inSR=4326`.
- **Seattle annexation:** Space Needle returns three cumulative polygons (Years 1869, 1886, 1883); take the minimum Year. The Wedgwood point returns a single 1953 polygon ("Sand Point District ... Lake City, Northgate, Wedgewood, Sand Point", Ordinance 81655), not the 1945 / Ordinance 73879 result recorded in WA-PROBES.md for "Wedgwood"; the earlier probe must have used a different point. The field list is longer than documented: also `Statute_Link`, `Ordinance_Link`, `Resolution`, `Resolution_Date`, `Resolution_Link`, `Clerk_File`, `Clerk_File_Link`, `Council_Bill`, `Council_Bill_Link`, `Amendment`, `GlobalID`.
- **Seattle parcels (PARCEL_GEO):** `ADDRESS` is padded with three spaces between the house number and the street (`400   BROAD ST`); `YR_BUILT_MAX` and `YR_RENOV_MAX` are strings; `LANDMARK` is `"Y"` or `null`. Wedgwood point: PIN 6844701790, "Rite-Aid Drugstore", built 1952, renovated 1990. Space Needle: PIN 1985200495, built 1961, renovated 2013, LANDMARK Y.
- **Seattle landmarks:** 30 point features in the envelope, returned in EPSG 4326 as requested. `EFF_DATE` is an epoch-millisecond integer and can be `null` (e.g. "Seattle-First National Bank"). Extra field `SE_ANNO_CAD_DATA` not listed in WA-PROBES.md.
- **USGS historical topos:** 31 catalog rows at the Space Needle (same set as WA-PROBES.md). The body is large (360 KB pretty-printed) because every row carries ~45 attributes; request only the needed `outFields` in production.
- **Macrostrat:** one unit with `t_age`/`b_age` (top/bottom age in Ma), `best_int_name`, `lith`, `descrip`, `macro_units`, `strat_names`.
- **Wikipedia REST summary:** all four pages return `coordinates`, `thumbnail`, `extract` and `extract_html`, plus `wikibase_item` (the Wikidata id).
- **Wikidata SPARQL (Seattle population):** three statements with point in time: 2010, 2018, 2020.
- **OpenFreeMap positron style:** Mapbox/MapLibre style version 8, 55 layers, sources `openmaptiles` and `ne2_shaded`, glyphs served from tiles.openfreemap.org. The style has no `name` key.
- **Rate limiting seen during capture:** sending the four Wikipedia REST summaries and the geosearch at the same instant got the geosearch a 429 ("You are making too many requests to the API"). The Wikidata query service was also returning 429 with the message "Aggressively rate-limiting to 1 req / min - this rule was created during active wdqs outage", so the dataset queries were spaced 65 s apart. The geosearch stayed 429 on retries at +12 s and +4 min and succeeded on the fourth attempt at +4.5 min, so the Wikipedia action API applies a longer per-client cool-down than the REST summary endpoint. Keep Wikimedia calls sequential, and back off for minutes, not seconds, on a 429.
- **Wikipedia geosearch:** 10 pages within 1 km of the Space Needle with `pageid`, `title`, `lat`, `lon`, `dist` (metres) and `primary`.
